arxiv-2012-03524.title: The Hausdorff measure of the range and level sets of Gaussian random fields with sectorial local nondeterminism
arxiv-2012-03524.creator: Cheuk Yin Lee
arxiv-2012-03524.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Cheuk Yin Lee. We determine the exact Hausdorff measure functions for the range and level sets of a class of Gaussian random fields satisfying sectorial local nondeterminism and other assumptions. We also establish a Chung-type law of the iterated logarithm. The results can be applied to the Brownian sheet, fractional Brownian sheets whose Hurst indices are the same in all directions, and systems of linear stochastic wave equations in one spatial dimension driven by space-time white noise or colored noise.

arxiv-2104-01603.description: Abstract The paper proposes a novel model assessment paradigm aiming to address shortcoming of posterior predictive p − p- values, which provide the default metric of fit for Bayesian structural equation modelling (BSEM). The model framework of the paper focuses on the approximate zero approach, according to which parameters that would before set to zero (e.g.

arxiv-2112-14176.title: Simulation-based spectral analysis of X-ray CCD data affected by photon pile-up
arxiv-2112-14176.creator: Tsubasa Tamba ∗, Hirokazu Odaka, Aya Bamba, Hiroshi Murakami, Koji Mori, Kiyoshi Hayashida, Yukikatsu Terada, Tsunefumi Mizuno, Masayoshi Nobukawa
arxiv-2112-14176.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Tsubasa Tamba ∗, Hirokazu Odaka, Aya Bamba, Hiroshi Murakami, Koji Mori, Kiyoshi Hayashida, Yukikatsu Terada, Tsunefumi Mizuno, Masayoshi Nobukawa. We have developed a simulation-based method of spectral analysis for pile-up affected data of X-ray CCDs without any loss of photon statistics. As effects of the photon pile-up appear as complicated nonlinear detector responses, we employ a detailed simulation to calculate the important processes in an X-ray observation including physical interactions, detector signal generation, detector readout, and a series of data reduction processes.

arxiv-2204-04522.title: Knowledge-Free Black-Box Watermark and Ownership Proof for Image Classification Neural Networks
arxiv-2204-04522.creator: Fangqi Li, Shilin Wang
arxiv-2204-04522.description: Abstract Watermarking has become a plausible candidate for ownership verification and intellectual property protection of deep neural networks. Regarding image classification neural networks, current watermarking schemes uniformly resort to backdoor triggers. However, injecting a backdoor into a neural network requires knowledge of the training dataset, which is usually unavailable in the real-world commercialization.

arxiv-2211-12233.title: Coronal seismology by slow waves in non-adiabatic conditions
arxiv-2211-12233.creator: Dmitrii Y. Kolotkov 1,∗
arxiv-2211-12233.description: Abstract Slow magnetoacoustic waves represent an important tool for probing the solar coronal plasma. The majority of seismological methods with slow waves are based on a weakly non-adiabatic approach, which assumes the coronal energy transport has only weak effects on the wave dynamics.

arxiv-2306-05452.title: On the Blackbody Spectrum of Kilonovae
arxiv-2306-05452.creator: Albert Sneppen
arxiv-2306-05452.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Albert Sneppen. The early spectra of the kilonova AT2017gfo have a remarkably smooth blackbody continuum, which reveals information on the thermal properties and radioactive heating within the ejecta. However, the widespread use of a single-temperature blackbody to fit kilonova data is theoretically invalid, because 1) the significant travel-time delays for a rapidly cooling surface result in a broad distribution of temperatures and 2) the relativistic Doppler correction varies across different surface elements.

arxiv-2404-10293.title: Orbital Angular Momentum Beam assisted High-Order Harmonic Generation in Semiconductor Materials
arxiv-2404-10293.creator: C. Granados, B. Kumar Das, M. F. Ciappina
arxiv-2404-10293.description: Abstract We investigate the use of light beams carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) in the context of high harmonic generation (HHG) within semiconductor crystals. Our contribution deals with the transfer and conservation of OAM in the strong-field regime, from the driving laser field to the generated harmonics.

arxiv-2407-00848.title: Ego-to-Exo: Interfacing Third Person Visuals from Egocentric Views in Real-time for Improved ROV Teleoperation
arxiv-2407-00848.creator: Adnan Abdullah, Ruo Chen, Ioannis Rekleitis, Md Jahidul Islam
arxiv-2407-00848.description: Abstract Underwater ROVs (Remotely Operated Vehicles) are unmanned submersible vehicles designed for exploring and operating in the depths of the ocean. Despite using high-end cameras, typical teleoperation engines based on first-person (egocentric) views limit a surface operator’s ability to maneuver the ROV in complex deep-water missions.

arxiv-2409-03942.title: Maximizing On-Bill Savings through Battery Management Optimization
arxiv-2409-03942.creator: Rene Carmona 1 , Xinshuo Yang 1 , Siddharth Bhela 2, Claire Zeng 1
arxiv-2409-03942.description: Abstract . In many power grids, a large portion of the energy costs for commercial and industrial consumers are set with reference to the coincident peak load, the demand during the maximum system-wide peak, and their own maximum peak load, the non-coincident peak load.

arxiv-2505-06834.title: Local stabilizability implies global controllability in catalytically-controlled reaction systems
arxiv-2505-06834.creator: Yusuke Himeoka, Shuhei A. Horiguchi, Naoto Shiraishi, Fangzhou Xiao, Tetsuya J. Kobayashi
arxiv-2505-06834.description: Abstract Controlling complex reaction networks is a fundamental challenge in the fields of physics, chemistry, biology, and systems engineering. Here, we prove a general principle for catalytically-controlled reaction systems with kinetics where the reaction order and the stoichiometric coefficient match: the local stabilizability of a given state implies global controllability within its stoichiometric compatibility class.

arxiv-2505-14774.title: Are magnetic fields in cosmic voids primordial?
arxiv-2505-14774.creator: Deepen Garg, Ruth Durrer, Jennifer Schober
arxiv-2505-14774.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Deepen Garg, Ruth Durrer, Jennifer Schober. The nature of magnetic fields in the voids of the large-scale structure of the Universe has been a multifaceted open puzzle for decades. On one hand, their origin is not clear with most of the magnetogenesis models using physics beyond the standard model in the early Universe, and on the other hand, their existence and potential role in explaining the spectra of TeV blazars have been intensely debated in the past decade.

arxiv-2511-16762.title: Radiative Neutrino Mass Generation and Dark Matter through Vector-like Leptons
arxiv-2511-16762.creator: Mohamed Amin Loualidi, Salah Nasri, Maximiliano A. Rivera
arxiv-2511-16762.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohamed Amin Loualidi, Salah Nasri, Maximiliano A. Rivera. This study presents a radiative three-loop framework for neutrino mass generation, employing an asymmetric Yukawa coupling between two new scalar S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) L SU(2)_{L} doublets and vector-like lepton doublets. Dark matter candidates arise from the scalar sector of one of the doublets and play a crucial role in the generation of neutrino masses through their nonzero scalar mixing. The singly charged scalar sector undergoes an analogous mixing structure.

pmc-10674482.title: ConGPS: A Smart Container Positioning System Using Inertial Sensor and Electronic Map with Infrequent GPS
pmc-10674482.creator: Shan Huang, Zihan Song, Hyung-Rim Choi, Jae-Joong Kim, Do-Myung Park, Byung-Kwon Park
pmc-10674482.description: Real-time global positioning is important for container-based logistics. However, a challenge in real-time global positioning arises from the frequency of both global positioning system (GPS) calls and GPS-denied environments during transportation. This paper proposes a novel system named ConGPS that integrates both inertial sensor and electronic map data.

pmc-12570759.title: CRISPR adaptation in Streptococcus thermophilus benefits from phage environmental DNA
pmc-12570759.creator: F. R. Croteau, J. Tran, A. P. Hynes
pmc-12570759.description: The CRISPR-Cas system is a bacterial adaptive immune system that protects against infection by phages: viruses that infect bacteria. To develop immunity, bacteria integrate spacers—fragments of the invading nucleic acids—into their CRISPR array to serve as the basis for sequence-targeted DNA cleavage.

pmc-12591798.title: Ultrasound-guided microwave ablation of granulomatous mastitis: An effective therapeutic tool
pmc-12591798.creator: Xiangyang Huang, Xinyi Wang, Ruai Li, Huiping Lyu, Xin Li, Yiling Wang, Lihui Zhang, Guorong Lyu
pmc-12591798.description: BackgroundGranulomatous mastitis is a chronic inflammatory breast condition characterized by non-caseating granulomas in the breast tissue, often requiring multidisciplinary approaches for accurate diagnosis and effective management. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided microwave ablation (MWA) for the treatment of granulomatous mastitis compared with surgical excision.

pmc-12607103.title: Joint associations of handgrip strength and functional disability with cognitive impairment in older adults
pmc-12607103.creator: Yuejun Li, Xueming Han, Sirui He, Xingying Chen, Lan Liu, Peiyi Li
pmc-12607103.description: BackgroundHandgrip strength (HGS) and functional disability may reflect interconnected biological processes contributing to functional decline. However, the extent to which their co-occurrence predicts cognitive impairment in aging populations remains unclear. This study investigated the joint association of low HGS and functional disability with cognitive impairment in a nationally representative cohort of older Chinese adults.

pmc-12708053.title: Lumbar endoscopic decompression in the presence of unexpected conjoined nerve root pathology: technical benefits and case illustrations
pmc-12708053.creator: Ralph J Mobbs, Edwin H Y Lui
pmc-12708053.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Conjoined nerve roots (CNRs) represent a common yet frequently underdiagnosed congenital anomaly of the lumbar spine that increases the risk of iatrogenic injury. We present two cases of incidentally discovered CNRs successfully managed with full endoscopic spine surgery (ESS). While often missed on preoperative imaging, ESS provides a distinct advantage in managing these variants due to its magnified, high-definition visualization through a minimally invasive approach.

pmc-12780268.title: Use of SEM-PLS analysis to predict sports injuries in professional football players through warehouse technology data
pmc-12780268.creator: Fan Cheng, Hisham Noori Hussain Al-Hashimy, Jinfang Yao
pmc-12780268.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Sports injuries (SP-INJ) substantially affect athlete health and team performance, underscoring the need for precise risk assessment in professional football. This study develops and tests an interpretable partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) injury-risk model that integrates the following constructs: body mass index (BMI), mechanical load (ML), training-program structure (TP), context-specific risk factors (RF), warehouse-technology effectiveness (WT), which is supported by Electronic Athlete Information System (EAIS), musculoskeletal development (MD), performance, and SP-INJ.

pmc-12983757.title: Dilemma of self-management among patients with diabetes in primary care settings in China: a qualitative study
pmc-12983757.creator: Feifei Jin, Wenjing Fang, Chen Li, Yuanyuan Zhang, Jian Zheng, Tianbing Wang
pmc-12983757.description: ObjectiveThis qualitative study aimed to explore the self-management dilemmas faced by patients with diabetes in Chinese primary care and collect suggestions for improvement.DesignQualitative methods are used in this study. Thematic analysis was used to analyse the transcripts.SettingFour primary care communities in Beijing. The interviews were conducted between April and August 2025.

pmc-13196750.title: Room-temperature spinor condensate in halide perovskite microcavity
pmc-13196750.creator: Takaya Inukai, Ryohei Shibano, Taiki Ogura, Tohki Inoue, Daichi Okada, Shun Takahashi, Kenichi Yamashita
pmc-13196750.description: A deeper understanding of room temperature polariton condensed phases is essential for advancing quantum applications. Spin degrees of freedom inherent in polariton particles manifest themselves in the form of spinor condensation, which has been demonstrated only at cryogenic temperatures in the past. Herein, we demonstrate room-temperature spinor polariton condensation in a lead-halide perovskite microcavity under nonresonant optical excitation.

pmc-13211493.title: Role of Fisetin in the Mammalian Reproductive System
pmc-13211493.creator: Yilong Chen, Xiaogang Huang, Zhihong Zhao, Ronggen Wang, Ruiyan Liu, Jinhao Chen, Li Li, Minhua Hu, Hengxi Wei, Shouquan Zhang
pmc-13211493.description: Simple SummaryMammalian reproductive health faces growing threats from pollution, lifestyle, and aging, leading to conditions like infertility. Current medical treatments can be complex and have side effects. Fisetin is a natural compound found in many fruits and vegetables, such as strawberries and apples.

pmc-13364018.title: Hydrothermal Humification for Producing Humic-like Acids and Nitrogen-Enriched Humic-like Acids from Recycled Wheat Straw CTMP Black Liquor
pmc-13364018.creator: Xiaoyue Xu, Yichen Liu, Jiangtao Hu, Junlong Song, Wenyuan Zhu
pmc-13364018.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The high-value utilization of non-wood pulping black liquor is of great significance for the sustainable development of the pulp and paper industry. In this study, concentrated black liquor, obtained from the five-time recycling of KOH-pretreated wheat straw chemi-thermomechanical pulp (CTMP), was used as the feedstock for the preparation of humic-like acids (HLAs) through hydrothermal humification by utilizing the enriched organic components and residual alkalinity. Urea was further introduced to synthesize nitrogen-enriched humic-like acids (N-HLAs).

pmc-13458171.title: Development and Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence-Based Two-Step Model for Automated Serum Quality Assessment in Clinical Laboratories
pmc-13458171.creator: Weixin Chen, Yuxuan Xiong, Chenxi Zhang, Zhifang Sui, Fengning Yang, Zikun Ma, B.M., Qinglin Liu, Yuexin Cui, Ran Han
pmc-13458171.description: BackgroundEnhancing pre-analytical QC in clinical laboratories and providing risk alerts is crucial for ensuring accurate test results for patients whose samples are affected by hemolysis, icterus, or lipemia. We evaluated a novel, self-developed artificial intelligence (AI) approach for assessing serum quality using a two-step deep learning YOLOv5–ResNet-50 architecture model and explored its performance under real-world laboratory conditions.

pmc-13552329.title: Antibiotic utilization pattern and its associated factors based on WHO AWaRe classification at a university hospital in the South of Thailand
pmc-13552329.creator: Sukrit Sawangpon, Saowalak Intasarat, Husna Chehtae, Slinna Chanmanee, Aunchittha Piromrak, Tanavij Pannoi
pmc-13552329.description: BackgroundAntibiotic overuse accelerates antimicrobial resistance (AMR), posing a major global health threat. The World Health Organization (WHO) AWaRe classification promotes rational antibiotic use, recommending that at least 60% of antibiotic consumption belongs to the Access group. This study evaluated antibiotic prescribing patterns and factors associated with Watch/Reserve antibiotic use in a Thai tertiary hospital.
